classifiedFindings.label: L-04
classifiedFindings.title: Privileged mintFor()/burn() ignore global paused + per-index disabled flags

classification.assetImpact: No asset theft or net inflation. mintFor() mints exactly 1 claim NFT 1:1 against a burned V1 NFT and is gated to authorizedMinters (only the trusted NFTMigrator is wired); burn() is gated to authorizedBurners. The defect is a kill-switch completeness gap, not an asset path: when the owner sets config.disabled = true (documented as 'new mints are blocked') or the contract is paused, the migrator path can still mint/burn the index.
attackPath: 1. Not externally attacker-executable: both entry points require authorizedMinters[msg.sender] / authorizedBurners[msg.sender], which only the trusted migrator holds.
2. Operator sets configs[index].disabled = true intending 'new mints blocked', or the pauser pauses the contract.
3. The migrator (trusted) calls mintFor(index, recipient); _executeMint's !paused / !disabled guards are absent on mintFor, so the mint proceeds anyway.
4. Result: the disabled/paused index is still mintable via the privileged path, contradicting documented semantics — but only the trusted minter benefits and supply stays 1:1 vs burned V1.
classification.likelihood: low - no permissionless trigger; requires the trusted migrator to act while an index is disabled/paused. Impact is semantic (incomplete kill switch), not financial.
classification.assumptions: Only the audited NFTMigrator is authorized as minter/burner (matches deployment); mints remain 1:1 against burned V1 NFTs.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner disables an index (or pauser pauses) AND the trusted migrator subsequently mints/burns that index.

classifiedFindings.justification: C4 High/Medium both require an asset-loss or protocol-availability path; neither exists here. There is no untrusted beneficiary, no net inflation (1:1 against burned V1), and no external attacker can reach mintFor/burn. The pause-bypass leg is deliberate-by-design (a pause-exempt migration primitive). The residual is the disabled-bypass: a Law-2 spec deviation from the documented 'new mints are blocked' semantics and a non-obvious owner footgun (an owner who disables an index would be surprised the migrator can still mint it). That is incorrect state-handling / spec-conformance, i.e. QA/Low under C4, not Medium. Carried at honest Low with faithfulness tag F-03 routed to the spec-conformance report so it is visible to the owner, not buried.

classifiedFindings.label: L-05
classifiedFindings.title: No on-chain invariant couples BalancerPoolerV2.batchDonationSize and Hook.ratio (missing batchDonationSize + ratio <= 100 guardrail)
classifiedFindings.scopeGuard: SURVIVING FRAMING IS THE UNLINKED-KNOBS / MISSING-ON-CHAIN-INVARIANT OPERATOR GUARDRAIL ONLY. The 'phUSD is unbacked / value can leak from the backing model' security claim is DEDUP-001 (hard-suppressed, OOS backing model per KI-1/KI-4, econ REFUTE-A: backing arithmetic unchanged from pre-story-034 baseline). It MUST NOT be re-introduced as a fresh security claim here.

classification.assetImpact: No in-protocol asset is placed at direct risk by the surviving leg. Two owner setters in two separate contracts (BalancerPoolerV2.batchDonationSize, cap 100; Hook.ratio, cap 50) have no on-chain linking invariant, so the owner can silently configure batchDonationSize + ratio > 100 — crossing the documented solvency-coupling boundary with no on-chain guard. The downstream backing consequence is the OOS, suppressed DEDUP-001 claim and is not asserted here.
attackPath: 1. No permissionless trigger (Tier-3 invariant-confirmed). Both setters are onlyOwner.
2. Owner sets BalancerPoolerV2.batchDonationSize to a value and, independently, Hook.ratio to a value whose sum exceeds 100.
3. Nothing on-chain rejects or links the two; the configuration silently violates the batchDonationSize + ratio <= 100 guardrail.

4. Operational hazard realized: configuration sits outside the safe envelope until the owner manually corrects it. (Any backing/solvency consequence is the suppressed DEDUP-001 OOS claim, not classified here.)
classification.likelihood: low - requires a specific owner misconfiguration across two contracts; no attacker involvement and no permissionless path.
classification.assumptions: The safe envelope batchDonationSize + ratio <= 100 is the intended coupling (story-034); the external phUSD backing layer is out of scope.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner independently configures the two knobs so their sum exceeds 100, with no on-chain invariant to catch it.

classifiedFindings.justification: Framed strictly as the operator guardrail, this is a missing on-chain invariant / non-obvious cross-contract owner footgun: a competent non-malicious owner would be surprised that two separately-capped knobs in two contracts can silently sum past the solvency boundary. Per Law 3 it is an in-scope operational hazard, but with no permissionless trigger and no in-protocol asset at direct risk it sits at C4 QA/Low (state/config handling + spec deviation), not Medium. It is NOT escalated on the back of the unbacked-phUSD claim, which is the suppressed DEDUP-001 (OOS backing model, backing arithmetic proven unchanged). Carried at Low with faithfulness tag F-02 to the spec-conformance report; the suppressed security claim is parked visibly in the sanitizer's DEDUP-001 record (Law 1).

classifiedFindings.label: L-06
classifiedFindings.title: pool()/unlockCallback single-sided sUSDS LP-add relies solely on off-chain keeper minBPT with no on-chain price reference (MEV sandwich)

classification.assetImpact: Protocol-custodied value leak: BPT minted to the dispatcher (protocol treasury) on the single-sided AddLiquidityKind.UNBALANCED join can be less than fair if the sUSDS/phUSD pool is skewed around the join. Loss falls on the protocol treasury, NOT on minters/users. Magnitude is bounded by (idealBPT - minBPT), where minBPT is the keeper-supplied floor.
attackPath: 1. Authorized keeper broadcasts pool(minBPT) to the public mempool (pool() is onlyAuthorizedPooler whenNotPaused nonReentrant; an external attacker cannot initiate it).
2. Attacker observes the pending tx and sandwiches it: skews the Balancer V3 sUSDS/phUSD pool price immediately before the single-sided join.

3. The join executes at the skewed price; the contract receives bptAmountOut >= minBPT but below the unskewed-fair amount because there is no on-chain price reference to tighten the floor beyond the off-chain minBPT.

4. Attacker reverses the skew after the join, capturing up to (idealBPT - minBPT) in value extracted from treasury BPT. The H-02 accumulate-then-dump design enlarges the single join and thus the extractable imbalance.
classification.likelihood: low-to-moderate - requires the conjunction of (a) keeper sets minBPT loosely relative to the true getIdealBPT() quote, (b) keeper broadcasts via a public (non-private) mempool, and (c) attacker wins the MEV race. Each is independently mitigable by the protocol.
classification.assumptions: Keeper sets minBPT with slack below idealBPT; keeper does not use a private relay (Flashbots); pool has enough depth-asymmetry for a profitable single-sided sandwich.
classification.externalRequirements: Public-mempool broadcast + a loose minBPT bound + a winning sandwich. With a tight minBPT (computed from the on-chain getIdealBPT()/queryAddLiquidityUnbalanced quote) or a private relay, extractable value approaches zero.

classifiedFindings.justification: This is the one genuine Low/Medium borderline, adjudicated rigorously. C4 Medium admits a 'value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements' even when gated by external conditions, so the mere presence of external requirements does not by itself disqualify Medium. The decisive Low factors are: (1) a functioning slippage control already exists — minBPT is a required, keeper-computed floor (default is NOT zero), so the defect is the ABSENCE OF AN ON-CHAIN PRICE CROSS-CHECK on an already-present off-chain bound, i.e. a hardening/defense-in-depth gap rather than a missing control; (2) the trigger is permissioned — an attacker cannot force pool(); they can only opportunistically sandwich a tx the keeper voluntarily broadcasts, and the keeper can defeat the entire vector with a private relay; (3) the loss magnitude is fully bounded by (idealBPT - minBPT) and is directly under protocol control — a competent keeper using the on-chain getIdealBPT() quote drives extractable value to ~0; (4) the value at risk is protocol-treasury BPT, not user funds, so no user asset is at risk; (5) project precedent — the structurally-identical L-03 (old AMM-swap leg) and the econ-scanner both rated this surface Low, and a self-audit must stay consistent and not inflate. Against Medium, the H-02 accumulate-then-dump amplification and the real (if bounded) treasury leak are acknowledged, but they only bite under the conjunction of a misconfigured/loose minBPT AND a public broadcast AND a won race — i.e. the residual collapses to operator-config robustness once the existing floor is used correctly. Net: a bounded, protocol-controllable, treasury-only, permissioned-trigger value leak with an already-present (if off-chain) mitigation sits below the Medium bar. Classified Low (L-06); recommend the cheap on-chain hardening of deriving/clamping minBPT against getIdealBPT() at call time and/or private-relay broadcast. Confidence is medium precisely because this is the borderline case.
classifiedFindings.borderlineResolution: Held at Low: existing off-chain slippage floor + permissioned (non-attacker-initiated) trigger + protocol-controllable bounded magnitude + treasury-only (no user) exposure + L-03 precedent keep it sub-Medium. Recommend on-chain minBPT derivation/clamp as remediation.

classifiedFindings.label: L-07
classifiedFindings.channel: main (Low footgun) -- may alternatively fold as a sub-item under the C-01 qa bundle (human review)
classifiedFindings.title: replaceDispatcher() carries stale per-index price to a new dispatcher whose primeToken may have different decimals (price re-denomination)

classification.assetImpact: Mis-scaled mint charge during the window between replaceDispatcher and a corrective setPrice. configs[index].price is a raw number whose denomination is defined by whichever dispatcher's primeToken is currently bound. Swapping an 18-dp prime-token dispatcher for one whose primeToken has fewer decimals (e.g. 6-dp) silently re-denominates the carried-over price: either mints revert (price now astronomically large in the new token's units -> availability impact) or, in the reverse direction, mints become near-free (price now negligible -> users obtain NFTs while the dispatcher receives ~0 backing).
attackPath: 1. Not attacker-initiated: replaceDispatcher is onlyOwner. The owner performs what looks like a like-for-like dispatcher swap.
2. The new dispatcher's primeToken has different decimals than the old one; configs[index].price persists unchanged across the swap.
3. _executeMint transfers `price` units of the NEW primeToken (IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, dispatcher, price)). The number is now denominated wrong.
4a. Lower-decimals new token: a stored 18-dp price is gigantic in 6-dp units -> safeTransferFrom reverts -> minting for that index is bricked until setPrice (availability), OR
4b. Higher-decimals new token: a stored 6-dp price is dust in 18-dp units -> near-free mints, under-backing the dispatcher, until the owner notices and calls setPrice.
classification.likelihood: low - requires the owner to (a) replace a dispatcher with one whose primeToken has different decimals AND (b) not immediately call setPrice. No attacker path; bounded to the corrective window.
classification.assumptions: Owner uses replaceDispatcher across dispatchers with mismatched primeToken decimals and does not atomically follow with setPrice.
classification.externalRequirements: A dispatcher swap to a different-decimals primeToken plus a delay before corrective setPrice.

classifiedFindings.justification: A non-obvious owner footgun (Law 3 in-scope, classified by impact rather than dismissed as malicious-admin/centralization): the name replaceDispatcher implies a like-for-like swap and gives no hint that price persists in NFTMinterV2 while its denomination is owned by the bound dispatcher's primeToken — a competent non-malicious owner would be surprised. Impact is bounded to the window before the corrective setPrice and is reachable only through an owner action with a delay, so it is C4 QA/Low (incorrect state-handling on a privileged config path), not Medium: there is no permissionless trigger and the worst case is a self-inflicted, owner-fixable mint revert (availability) or a brief near-free-mint window. Kept as a fresh Low footgun (L-07) with safe-config guidance (re-set price atomically within replaceDispatcher, or restrict swaps to same-decimals prime tokens). It is a DISTINCT aspect from C-01 (general re-pointing of token/metadata under existing holders), which does not cover the price re-denomination sub-issue; flagged for human review on whether to fold it under the C-01 qa bundle.
classifiedFindings.ledgerAdjacency: C-01 (distinct aspect; classifier may fold as a C-01 sub-item)

classifiedFindings.label: Q-05
classifiedFindings.title: nonReentrant is not the first modifier on pool()/the hook-guarded entry (defense-in-depth)

classification.assetImpact: None demonstrated. Modifier ordering only; no exploitable reentrancy found this run (CEI invariant PASS, NFTMinterV2 reentrancy lead refuted as L-01). Placing nonReentrant last means preceding modifiers (onlyAuthorizedPooler, whenNotPaused) run before the guard engages; neither makes an external call this run, so there is no concrete attack surface.
attackPath: 1. No external interaction exists in the modifiers preceding nonReentrant on the current code, so there is no reentrant entry to exploit.
2. The item is purely a defense-in-depth hardening: reorder nonReentrant to first so the guard is established before any future modifier that might make an external call.
classification.likelihood: n/a - no exploit path; purely preventative.

classifiedFindings.justification: Pure defense-in-depth / code-quality observation with no demonstrated impact: no preceding modifier performs an external call, so there is no reentrancy path to exploit. Under C4 this is QA (style/robustness), not Low-with-impact and certainly not Medium/High. Reorder nonReentrant to the first modifier as hardening. Kept in the QA bundle (Q-05).
